reason: The contract requires abs(actual[i] - atan(x[i])) <= 1e-6 with zero relative tolerance for EVERY finite FP16 input, and explicitly states a single verdict over the entire legal domain; approximations are permitted only if the tolerance holds throughout. The exhaustive probe over all 31743 positive finite FP16 values (atan is odd, negatives symmetric) shows max absolute error vs the FP64 reference of 5.03277156949089e-06 at x=0.6220703125 — over 5x the tolerance — confirming c1. The boundary probe (c2) confirms 186 of 310 values near |x|=0.66 and 2.414 violate the tolerance (lower branch 5.03e-06, middle branch 3.31e-06), and the upper-branch probe (c3) confirms 516 of 14848 values with |x|>=3 violate it (max 2.14e-06 at x=3.005859375). Root cause: the truncated decimal coefficients (-122.9, 485.4, 24.86, etc.) make the FP32 rational approximation inherently incapable of 1e-6 accuracy across the domain, not merely FP32 rounding. This is not a contract-permitted deviation: the tolerance is fixed at 1e-6 absolute on real-arithmetic targets, and these inputs are explicitly in the stated domain. Confirmed, in-scope, scope-evidence tied to problem.txt (the operative contract here, since the artifact provides no test.py/get_inputs narrowing the domain). Reject.
